description: Solo full-stack developer building an interactive space museum and AI storytelling web application dedicated to NASA's historic rovers, landers, and equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Combining real NASA mission telemetry, surface maps, and an AI radio persona mode.
summary: Silent Sentinels is an interactive 3D aerospace museum and storytelling platform dedicated to NASA's historic rovers, landers, and robotic pioneers resting across the Moon and Mars. Built with WebGL (Three.js and globe.gl), the application lets users explore real orbital landing coordinates, inspect official NASA 2 km lunar heritage protection zones, scrub across six decades of space exploration (1967–2026), and listen to synthesized Black Box audio logs framed with authentic NASA Quindar radio tones. An integrated Gemini-powered AI Radio Comms module allows students and space enthusiasts to converse directly with each spacecraft's historical persona and a NASA Flight Historian. By transforming static mission archives into an immersive, living museum, Silent Sentinels preserves humanity's off-world technological heritage and inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
Silent Sentinels is an interactive 3D aerospace museum and digital heritage platform created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars").

What It Does & How It Works:

Across the basalt plains of the Moon and the rust deserts of Mars rest the silent robotic and human-crewed pioneers that expanded humanity's reach into the solar system. Silent Sentinels transforms static mission records into an explorable 3D planetary museum featuring:

1. Interactive 3D Planetary Globes (Moon & Mars): Built with WebGL (Three.js & globe.gl), allowing users to rotate, zoom, and fly directly to verified landing coordinates (latitude/longitude) of 8 iconic relics—Apollo 11 "Eagle", Apollo 15 LRV-1, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, Ingenuity, and Viking 1—plus official NASA 2 km Lunar Heritage Protection buffer zones.

2. Chronological Expedition Timeline (1967–2026): Users can scrub through six decades of space exploration or launch a Guided Expedition Tour that flies chronologically from relic to relic.

3. 3-Act Documentary Storytelling & Black Box Audio Logs: Each spacecraft features structured narrative chapters, real-time Earth–Planet light-time delay calculations, warranty vs. survival analytics, and synthesized voice playback framed with authentic NASA Quindar radio tones.

4. Deep-Space AI Radio Comms: Powered by Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash), users can open a simulated radio link to converse directly with each spacecraft's historical persona or ask a NASA Flight Historian technical questions about its scientific instruments and discoveries.

Intended Impact & Benefits:

Designed for students, educators, and space enthusiasts, Silent Sentinels makes planetary science intuitive and emotionally engaging. By visualizing exact landing sites alongside NASA's heritage preservation guidelines, it raises awareness about protecting off-world historical artifacts as humanity returns to the Moon under the Artemis program.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend & 3D Graphics: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, globe.gl

- Audio & AI Integration: Web Audio API (procedural Quindar radio tone synthesis), Web Speech API, Google Gemini API (gemini-2.5-flash)

- Deployment & Version Control: Vercel, GitHub (https://github.com/Salamathss/silent-sentinels-nasa-2026)

Design & Creativity Considerations:

We prioritized high-contrast editorial legibility ("Dark Luxury" museum aesthetic), authentic mission telemetry formatting, and dual-persona AI grounding so every conversation remains scientifically accurate while feeling like a live deep-space transmission.
